summary: The proof is correct. The prescribed cap law identifies the full open support interval of each affine functional and gives a positive constant derivative there. The slice-length argument then forces the convex body to be a parallelogram whose edges are parallel to that functional's level lines. Applying this to three pairwise nonparallel linear parts requires three distinct edge directions, contradicting the two edge directions of a nondegenerate parallelogram. The stated joint-realization consequence follows immediately.
